## Rates

## Was v2 an improvement?

No measurable improvement — and none was needed. The baseline 
prompt-v1 already achieved 100% catch rate and 0% false alarm 
rate across all 3 baseline runs and all 12 cases. Prompt-v2 
produced identical results. The SOC 2 context sentence made 
one notable difference: in run 4 case-07, Copilot explicitly 
named the SOC 2 concern ("creating a SOC 2 concern") where 
runs 1-3 only noted "plausible exposure." This shows the 
additional context sharpened the framing of the finding 
without changing the verdict.

## Confidence Statement

12 cases × 3 baseline runs = 36 observations.
Defect cases: 9. Clean cases: 3.
The model caught every defect in every run with zero false alarms.
The ceiling effect (100% baseline) means v2 could not show 
improvement on catch rate. A harder eval set with ambiguous 
cases would be needed to distinguish v1 from v2 meaningfully.
At this sample size and with a perfect baseline, I cannot claim 
v2 is better — only that it is not worse, and that it produces 
more SOC 2-specific framing on data-exposure cases.

## Additional runs 5 and 6 (both v2)

Runs 5 and 6 confirmed the run 4 results exactly.
All 9 defect cases caught, all 3 clean cases clean across both 
additional runs. The model is highly consistent on these cases.
